job.title: Engineering & Projects Innovation Manager
job.description:
Engineering Manager – Projects & Innovation

Position purpose and primary objectives:
The Engineering Projects & Innovation Manager provides strategic and technical leadership across the Company's engineering and research & development (R&D) project portfolio. This role is responsible for planning, developing, and delivering innovative engineering solutions that enhance product performance, operational efficiency, and market competitiveness.
Reporting to the General Manager Operations, this position leads a multidisciplinary team to translate strategic innovation goals into viable projects through executing and guiding each phase from concept development and prototyping through to validation and implementation.
This role is to instil engineering excellence, project discipline, and effective collaboration across teams to drive technical advancement whilst maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, and financial performance. The Engineering Manager - Projects & Innovation is central to shaping The Company’s engineering capabilities and contributing to their reputation as an industry leader in trenchless pipeline rehabilitation technologies.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Leadership & Governance
  • Provide leadership and direction for the Engineering Projects and Innovation team, ensuring alignment with company’s strategic and operational objectives.
  • Contribute to operational planning and decision-making, supporting the GM Operations in achieving business performance and innovation goals.
  • Build and develop a high-performing team that is ready to deliver on current and future projects.
  • Establish and maintain a structured project governance process, covering the complete project lifecycle.
  • Prepare and present project performance reports, budgets, and technical updates to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, and accountability across all engineering activities.

Engineering Project Development & Delivery
  • Lead the delivery of R&D and engineering projects from concept through to handover to the Commercial team, ensuring technical integrity, schedule adherence, and budget control.
  • Oversee and active involvement throughout the planning and execution of engineering design, testing, validation, and implementation activities.
  • Coordinate cross-functional input from Operations, Quality, Purchasing and Commercial to ensure successful integration of new technologies and products.
  • Implement consistent project management and engineering standards to drive predictability, repeatability, and efficiency in project delivery.
  • Manage internal and external stakeholders to ensure clear communication, alignment, and customer satisfaction.
  • Ensure all projects achieve defined outcomes in performance, safety and quality.

Innovation & Technology Research & Development
  • Drive a culture of innovation within the engineering team, encouraging creativity, continuous improvement, and applied research.
  • Identify and develop emerging technologies, materials, and processes that support further innovation across company’s products.
  • Collaborate with Parent group companies, suppliers, and research facilities to support joint development and testing initiatives.
  • Oversee the design, fabrication, and evaluation of prototypes and trials that enhance operational performance aimed at reducing installation costs.
  • Support the capture and protection of any intellectual property developed within the company.

Operational Excellence & Risk Management
  • Establish and maintain best practice project management methodologies across all engineering and innovation activities.
  • Develop, monitor, and control project budgets, schedules, and resource allocations.
  • Identify and manage technical, operational, and commercial risks associated with engineering projects.
  • Drive continuous improvement in engineering processes, documentation, and system utilisation.
  • Ensure all projects comply with internal governance frameworks and relevant legislative or client requirements.

Quality, Safety & Environment (QSE)
  • Champion a culture of safety, quality, and environmental responsibility across all engineering operations.
  • Ensure all projects and activities comply with company’s Integrated Management System (IMS).
  • Lead regular reviews of engineering risk assessments, incident investigations, and corrective actions.
  • Promote proactive health, safety, and environmental practices and continuous improvement in QSE performance.
Skills & Qualifications:
Essential
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical or Industrial Engineering (or related discipline).
  • Minimum 8 years’ experience in engineering project management, product development, or R&D within manufacturing, infrastructure, or industrial environments.
  • Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering teams through complex project lifecycles.
  • Demonstrated capability in project governance, budgeting, scheduling, and reporting.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk management skills.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Proficient in project management software and engineering documentation systems.

Desirable
  • Postgraduate qualifications in Engineering Management, Project Management, or Business Administration.
  • Experience working in a multinational corporate environment.
  • Exposure to trenchless technologies, pipeline rehabilitation, or related infrastructure sectors.
  • Experience with digital engineering platforms or innovation management systems.

Key Competencies & Attributes:
  • Strategic and systems thinker with a strong engineering foundation.
  • Demonstrated leadership ability to inspire, mentor, and develop technical teams.
  • Strong commercial awareness with an ability to balance innovation, cost, and performance outcomes.
  • Collaborative and confident communicator, able to build relationships across functions and geographies.
  • Highly organised, disciplined, and results-focused.
  • Resilient, proactive, and adaptable to changing project priorities.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, quality, and workplace safety.

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Procurement & Contract Officer to support procurement activities, contract management and stakeholder engagement within a busy and process-driven environment.

About The Company
Our client is a well-established organisation operating within a structured and complex environment, with a strong focus on effective procurement, contract management and sound governance processes.

Role Overview
This role will provide support across general procurement and contract management activities, including contract variations, tender processes, record keeping and stakeholder engagement. The successful candidate will be confident following established processes, exercising sound judgement and taking ownership of tasks through to completion.

About the Person
We are looking for someone who is highly organised, proactive and delivery-focused, with excellent attention to detail and a strong ability to follow established processes. You will have experience in procurement and/or contract management and be confident working independently while engaging effectively with a range of stakeholders.
Government experience is not essential, with comprehensive training available for the successful candidate.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support general procurement and contract management activities.
  • Manage contract variations and associated processes.
  • Maintain accurate procurement, contract and administrative records.
  • Support tender processes, including obtaining and assessing quotes from the market.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensure procurement and contract processes are completed accurately and in accordance with established procedures.
  • Provide administrative and operational support across procurement activities.
  • Take ownership of tasks and ensure deliverables are completed within required timeframes.
Skills, Knowledge and Experience
  • Working With Children Check (WWCC) and National Police Clearance are required.
  • Demonstrated experience in procurement and/or contract management.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Strong ability to follow established processes and procedures.
  • Sound judgement and decision-making skills.
  • Strong organisational, administrative and record-keeping capabilities.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to work independently, proactively and take ownership of tasks.
  • A delivery-focused approach with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills are desirable.
  • Government experience is desirable but not essential.

job.title: Senior IT Governance Specialist
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior IT Governance Specialist to support effective IT governance, risk management, assurance and compliance activities within a complex organisation.

About The Company
Our client is a large and well-established organisation with a complex operating environment and a strong focus on effective governance, risk management and continuous improvement.

Role Overview
This role will be responsible for supporting and enhancing IT governance frameworks, policies, processes and assurance activities. You will work closely with key stakeholders across the organisation to monitor risks, support governance committees and boards, coordinate audit activities and provide advice on effective IT governance practices.

About the Person
We are looking for a governance professional with strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills. You will have experience working across IT governance, risk, assurance, audit or compliance and be confident developing governance documentation, managing risk registers and working with senior stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design, implement and maintain IT governance frameworks and processes.
  • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of IT governance practices.
  • Support IT risk management activities and maintain risk registers.
  • Liaise with stakeholders regarding risk updates and governance committee actions.
  • Draft and maintain governance standards, policies, procedures and terms of reference.
  • Conduct research and analysis to support governance processes and reporting.
  • Coordinate and track internal audit activities and actions.
  • Provide advice and support to stakeholders on IT governance matters.
  • Promote a culture of effective governance, risk management and continuous improvement.
  Skills, Knowledge and Experience
  • Relevant qualifications or professional certifications in governance, risk, audit, compliance, information technology or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience in IT governance, risk, assurance, audit or compliance.
  • Strong understanding of governance frameworks, policies, risk management and assurance practices.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare high-quality governance documentation.
  • Strong analytical and research skills with excellent attention to detail.
  • Proven ability to engage and collaborate with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Experience maintaining risk registers and coordinating governance or audit actions.
  • Experience working within a higher education or similarly complex public-sector environment is highly desirable.

  • Influence strategy, customer outcomes and operational performance
  • Lead skilled technical teams across complex managed services

Insync Solutions is a specialist Australian technology consultancy focused on Identity & Access Management (IAM), Cyber Security and Cloud Solutions. Partnering with leading vendors including Microsoft, SailPoint, Okta, OpenText and Ping Identity we help organisations solve complex security and technology challenges. Our highly experienced consultants deliver solutions across the full project lifecycle, from strategy and design through to implementation and ongoing support, while remaining at the forefront of emerging technologies through continuous learning and development.

Working closely with technical specialists, customers and company leadership, you will play a pivotal role in driving service excellence, customer satisfaction and operational performance across the business.

job.title: Head of People & Culture
job.description:
Lead the people strategy behind GMCU's next chapter


Shepparton and Surrounds, Regional VIC | Senior Leadership Team

Not every Head of People & Culture role offers the opportunity to genuinely transform an organisation.

This one does.

GMCU is a proud member-owned financial institution with over 70 years of history serving communities across regional Victoria. We've built our reputation on trust, authenticity and putting people before profits. As we continue to evolve, we're embarking on the next phase of our organisational journey, modernising how we work, strengthening leadership capability, and creating a high-performance culture that will support future growth.

The Opportunity
Over recent years, GMCU has invested significantly in building the foundations of its People & Culture function.
The next challenge is different.
We're looking for a leader who can elevate organisational capability, drive cultural maturity, and partner closely with senior leaders to drive strategic objectives.
The successful candidate will play a critical role in helping GMCU continue its transition from a traditional operating model to a more contemporary, digitally enabled organisation.

What You'll Be Responsible For
  • Leading GMCU's People & Culture strategy and roadmap
  • Driving organisation-wide performance, capability and leadership initiatives
  • Partnering with executives to support business transformation and change
  • Enhancing employee engagement, culture and retention outcomes
  • Leading workforce planning, talent attraction and succession strategies
  • Providing strategic advice on employee relations, industrial relations and workplace legislation
  • Championing workplace safety, wellbeing and inclusion
  • Developing frameworks, policies and people practices that support organisational growth
  • Contributing to Senior Leadership Team discussions and strategic decision-making 

What Success Looks Like
The number one priority for this role is clear:

Building a strong culture and workforce capability that enables GMCU to achieve its strategic growth objectives.

You'll help leaders set clear expectations, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and create an environment where people can do their best work while remaining connected to GMCU's values and community purpose.

About You
We're open-minded about industry background.
What matters most is your ability to influence, lead change and build capability.
You'll bring:
  • Significant experience leading people strategy within a complex organisation
  • A track record of successfully driving organisational change and cultural transformation
  • Strong capability in performance management, leadership development and workforce planning
  • Experience partnering with executives and boards on strategic people matters
  • Deep understanding of employment legislation, industrial relations and WHS
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and influencing skills
  • Tertiary qualifications in HR, Organisational Psychology, Business or a related discipline
Experience in organisational development, leadership capability, behavioural science or organisational psychology will be highly regarded.

Why Join GMCU?
This is more than a People & Culture leadership role.
It's an opportunity to shape the future of an organisation that genuinely values people, community and purpose.
You'll enjoy:
  • Senior Leadership Team membership
  • A highly visible role with meaningful organisational influence
  • The opportunity to lead significant transformation initiatives
  • Employee loan and banking benefits
  • Professional development opportunities
  • A values-driven culture focused on making a difference in local communities

Location
This position will be based in Shepparton. Given the highly collaborative nature of the role, we're seeking a leader who is committed to being embedded within the region and present with our people and leadership team.

Relocation support may be considered for an exceptional candidate.

  • Advise senior leaders on complex procurement and contracting strategies
  • Work with government and industry to deliver high-impact commercial outcomes

Salary
SS/SM1 – Salary Range $144,421 + superannuation per annum

Term
2-year fixed term contract


About the Company

What We Offer
  • Work that matters – impact that shapes South Australia’s future
  • Flexible working arrangements that support life and career
  • Salary packaging options
  • Discounted gym membership
  • Supportive learning & career development
  • Employee Assistance Program for you and your family

Who we are
At the Department of Treasury and Finance (DTF), we’re building a world-class Treasury for South Australia – one that’s innovative, collaborative and future-focused.
We’re South Australia’s lead agency for economic, digital and financial policy outcomes. Our work touches every corner of the state, from enabling frontline services to driving digital transformation. And we do it all with one purpose: to make life better for the people who call South Australia home.
The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) enables a more connected, secure and digital government so that South Australian Government agencies can better serve our community. We do this by leading the State’s technology, cyber security and digital government strategies, and by delivering resilient, innovative ICT, digital and cyber security services, platforms and critical infrastructure that are accessible, trusted and secure.
One of four Directorates in the Branch, Governance, Portfolio and Business Operations provides strategic, governance and business support services that enable OCIO to deliver on its priorities and outcomes. The directorate brings together specialist functions including strategic advice, program and portfolio governance oversight and reporting, procurement, communications, engagement and change management, as well as business operations including administration, finance, and workforce operations support. By providing centralised leadership, oversight and support functions, the directorate helps drive organisational alignment, accountability and effective service delivery, and helps ensure OCIO is well-positioned to deliver effective services and value across government.

The Senior Manager, Commercial, Procurement and Contract Administration is OCIO's lead commercial advisor, driving strategic procurement and contracting outcomes across complex ICT, digital and cyber security initiatives. Leading a specialist team, the role is responsible for delivering strategic commercial outcomes that maximise value, manage risk and support OCIO’s priorities and major government initiatives.

The position provides senior leadership across procurement, contract administration and commercial strategy, working closely with government agencies, industry partners and key stakeholders to deliver best-practice sourcing and contract management outcomes. Through strong stakeholder engagement and commercial expertise, the role supports the successful delivery of large-scale digital and technology initiatives while ensuring robust governance, compliance and value-for-money results.

  • Monitor commercial and procurement activities, ensuring accurate reporting, compliance, effective risk management and the timely resolution of complex enquiries.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, industry partners and suppliers to support collaboration and successful program delivery.
  • Foster a culture of service excellence, professionalism and continuous improvement.
  • Shape the commercial strategy underpinning major government digital, ICT and cyber security initiatives.

Essential Experience
  • Australian Citizenship is required and the ability to obtain and maintain a National Security Clearance.
  • Significant experience negotiating complex commercial contracts and agreements.
  • Demonstrated experience developing sourcing strategies, conducting market analysis and implementing contract management frameworks.
  • Strong commercial acumen gained within government or other large, complex organisations.
  • Proven ability to analyse complex issues, develop practical solutions and negotiate successful outcomes.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience, with the ability to motivate, develop and lead high-performing teams.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across all levels of an organisation and with external partners.
  • Experience preparing complex reports, policies, business cases and strategic documentation involving sensitive or high-profile matters.

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
Join Resolve in a key EA role combining executive support, stakeholder engagement, projects and business improvement. 
 

  • Newly created EA role partnering with two senior Directors 

  • Shape the role and become a trusted partner to the leadership team 

  • Bring structure, ideas and smarter ways of working to a growing firm 
     

Resolve is a modern family law firm that approaches things differently. Based in North Adelaide, the firm is known for strategic, practical and human-centered legal support and a genuine focus on doing things better for clients and for its people.  

Resolve is growing and is looking for an experienced Executive Assistant to join in a newly created role, supporting its Executive Director and Managing Director. 
 

Role Overview 

This is a newly created Executive Assistant role offering the opportunity to build a genuine partnership with two senior leaders and help shape how they work. As owners of the business, the Directors are closely aligned on strategy and direction, but bring different working styles to how they operate day to day and you will need to adapt your approach to each. 

One Director thinks in big picture, strategic terms, and will value someone who can help turn ideas into clear actions, bring structure to a busy schedule and create space for focused strategic thinking. The other works more closely across operational detail and will rely on you to manage a high volume of activity, coordinate leadership meetings, track actions and help drive accountability. 

You will need to understand how each Director works and adapt your approach accordingly, while having the confidence to ask questions, sense check priorities and respectfully challenge when appropriate. Alongside executive support, the role will include project coordination, stakeholder engagement and opportunities to improve systems, processes and ways of working. 
 

About the Person 

You are an experienced Executive Assistant who thrives on building trusted partnerships with the leaders you support. You are highly organised and naturally proactive, anticipating needs before they arise and bringing clarity, structure and follow-through to competing priorities. You enjoy creating order from complexity and are equally comfortable managing day-to-day operations while thinking several steps ahead. 

You exercise sound judgement, knowing when to take ownership, when to seek direction and when to respectfully challenge or offer a different perspective. You have a continuous improvement mindset, are curious about smarter ways of working and enjoy leveraging technology, systems and processes to create lasting efficiencies. Most importantly, you build trust quickly, remain calm under pressure and are exceptionally detail-oriented. You take pride in enabling others to perform at their best while contributing to the long-term success of the business. 
 

Key Responsibilities  

  • Manage complex diaries, inboxes, meetings and competing priorities across two Directors. 

  • Anticipate upcoming requirements and proactively keep both Directors organised and prepared. 

  • Coordinate leadership meetings, agendas, minutes, actions and follow-up. 

  • Manage stakeholder communication and act as a trusted point of contact on behalf of the Directors. 

  • Help translate ideas and discussions into clear actions, priorities and outcomes. 

  • Support projects and business improvement initiatives across the firm. 

  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes and introduce more efficient ways of working. 

  • Prepare correspondence, presentations, reports, briefing information and other executive documentation. 

  • Coordinate travel, events and other executive requirements as needed. 

  • Maintain absolute discretion when dealing with confidential and sensitive information. 

     

Skills, Knowledge and Experience  

  • Demonstrated experience as an Executive Assistant, Senior Personal Assistant or similar support for senior leaders. 

  • Strong diary, inbox and priority management skills. 

  • Confidence supporting multiple executives with different personalities and working styles. 

  • Highly proactive with the ability to anticipate needs rather than wait for direction. 

  • Strong judgement and the confidence to respectfully challenge or push back when appropriate. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

  • Strong stakeholder management skills and a professional, polished approach. 

  • Tech savvy with an interest in using systems and technology to improve efficiency. 

  • Adaptable and calm when priorities change or workloads increase. 

  • Professional services or legal experience will be highly regarded but is not essential. 
     

Culture of the business: 

Resolve is a modern and progressive family law firm with a strong focus on its clients, its people and continuing to evolve the way it works. It is a busy and agile environment, with a leadership team that is open to new ideas, technology and smarter ways of working. Collaboration and accountability are important, alongside a genuine willingness to listen to ideas and continually improve. This will suit someone who enjoys being part of a professional, forward-thinking business where they can contribute and make an impact. 
 

For more information, please contact Joanne Murtagh 0489 279 011 OR Elena Bacon 0483 915 113 
 

Please note – all applicant resumes must be submitted in Word format only.

job.title: Account Manager – Corporate Services Recruitment
job.description:
The Opportunity 
If you're an experienced agency recruiter, you'll know opportunities like this don't come along very often. 

Due to continued national growth, Harrison McMillan is looking for an experienced recruiter to join the high performing Recruitment Services team and take ownership of one of our established Corporate Services recruitment desks. 

This isn't a cold desk.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Harrison McMillan has the privilege of partnering with Hepatitis SA to appoint their next Chief Executive Officer.

About Hepatitis SA
Hepatitis SA is the lead community-based, not-for-profit organisation responding to viral hepatitis, primarily hepatitis B and hepatitis C, in South Australia.

The organisation provides education, peer education, information, referral and support services for people affected by viral hepatitis, people at risk, health and welfare professionals, and the broader community. Hepatitis SA is also a Needle and Syringe Program secondary site and operates harm reduction peer services across various NSP sites in metropolitan Adelaide.

With a committed team, strong sector relationships and a community-led approach, Hepatitis SA plays an important role in public health, harm reduction, advocacy and providing services for priority populations.

About the role
Reporting to the Board, the CEO will lead the day-to-day management and implementation of the strategic direction of Hepatitis SA.

This is a broad, hands-on role spanning service delivery, advocacy, funding and financial management, people management and stakeholder engagement, and advising the Board on policy, strategic and operational direction, organisational risk and finances.

The incoming CEO will build on strong organisational foundations while strengthening funding sustainability, systems and processes and impact reporting

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead Hepatitis SA’s operations, programs and people
  • Ensure services remain responsive to communities affected by viral hepatitis
  • Oversee education, peer education, support and harm reduction programs
  • Manage budgets, grants, funding submissions, acquittals, tenders and reporting
  • Build strong relationships with funders, government, sector partners and community stakeholders
  • Represent Hepatitis SA in local, state and national forums
  • Advise the Board re strategy, governance, risk, and budget planning and monitoring
  • Lead and support a small, diverse team, including peer workers
  • Strengthen systems, policies, documentation and organisational processes
  • Communicate the impact of Hepatitis SA’s work to funders, partners and the broader community

What we’re looking for:
  • Experience: Senior leadership experience in health, human services, community, not-for-profit or related settings
  • Financial Capability: Strong skills in budgeting, grants, acquittals, funding reports and tenders
  • Governance Knowledge: Experience working effectively with a Board
  • Community Understanding: Appreciation of health promotion, harm reduction lived experience and peer-led programs
  • Ability to Navigate Complexity: Comfortable operating in challenging environments with the ability to work autonomously, exercise sound judgement, and navigate complexity with confidence.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Leadership Style: Practical, inclusive, non-judgemental and able to build trust with diverse communities
  • Flexibility: Ability to work flexibly and undertake some intrastate and interstate travel

Benefits:
  • Meaningful Impact: Lead work that directly supports people affected by viral hepatitis
  • Strong Foundations: Join a respected organisation with experienced staff and sector relationships
  • Sector Influence: Represent Hepatitis SA across local, state and national forums
  • Purpose-Led Work: Contribute to hepatitis B and C elimination goals, with a focus on equity and no-one left behind
  • Salary Packaging: Salary packaging arrangements are available
  • Flexible Working: WFH options may apply after the first 12 months, subject to performance and policy

Why join Hepatitis SA?
This is an opportunity to lead a respected, community-based organisation with deep community connections and an important role in South Australia’s public health landscape.

The coming years will be important for Hepatitis SA, with new National Strategies, a changing funding environment, ongoing advocacy and continued work toward the elimination of hepatitis B and hepatitis C as public health threats.

This role will suit a leader who is both strategic and practical; someone who can build on what is already working well while strengthening and evolving the organisation for the future.

If you are ready to bring your leadership, community focus and strategic capability to Hepatitis SA, please visit harrisonmcmillan.com.au or click APPLY NOW. We request applications include a CV and Cover Letter outlining your interest and suitability for the role.  A position description is available upon request. Please note that the successful applicant will be required to undertake a police check. 

For confidential enquiries, please contact Tamara Chambers – Client Delivery Lead on 0468039108

Harrison McMillan and Hepatitis SA are committed to an inclusive recruitment process. Applications are encouraged from people with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with lived experience, and people from communities affected by viral hepatitis.
